summary: The first live attempt selected the wrong service route because ignoring user configuration also discarded the configured provider. The attempt is rejected and retained. The repair preserves only the existing service route/model while retaining fresh contexts and disabled tools; no new proxy or service is introduced.
findings: The final durable ledger records six invocations: five failed before output and the sixth was interrupted. The earlier progress observation of four was superseded as calls completed before interruption. No interpretation accuracy evidence was produced.
Stop on provider unavailability instead of spending the remaining initial-role allowance on the same access failure.
Whitelist configured provider/model settings, exclude hooks, MCP servers and developer instructions, and set provider transport retry counts to zero.
Code review also found that candidates without a distinguishing witness might never execute Java. Add direct generated-Java/Python probe verification for every successfully compiled reading.
Preserve ordered candidate IDs on comparisons and do not mark a failed reconstruction complete. Feed round-trip diagnostics into subsequent refinement.
These are implementation repairs. A successful later live run still cannot supply independent legal adjudication.
